name: Replicate

modes.label: Private Cog CPU model
modes.note: Private models and deployments bill setup + idle + active instance time, per second. After traffic stops an instance idles 'for a few minutes' before scaling to min_instances (0 by default), and that idle tail is billed. Failed and canceled runs are billed for private models and deployments. Same applies to all serverless-* GPU modes (unless running a public model or a fast-booting fine-tune, which bill active time only).

modes.label: Multi-GPU / H200 (committed spend)
modes.note: Listed per node: A100 4x $20.16/h, 8x $40.32/h; H100 2x $10.98, 4x $21.96, 8x $43.92; H200 1x $5.49, 2x $10.98, 4x $21.96, 8x $43.92; L40S 4x $14.04, 8x $28.08. Per-GPU rate equals the 1x rate. Capacity needs a committed-spend contract (commitment size not published).

plans.name: Usage
plans.note: Prepaid credit required for accounts created since 2025-07-16: buy credit upfront, usage is deducted; purchased credit expires 1 year after purchase and is non-refundable; auto-reload optional (min threshold $5, min reload balance $15). At $0 balance new work is blocked and running infrastructure is shut down. Pre-July-2025 accounts may still be billed monthly in arrears.

caveats: Public inference charges only processing (some by output/token); private custom Cog models charge setup + idle + active dedicated instance time. Fast-booting fine-tunes are special active-only exceptions.
Private CPU model deployment is an alt to interactive VM. GPUs include their hosts; do not double-count host CPU/RAM. Several multi-GPU and H200 SKUs require committed-spend contracts.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
GPU modes grafted from the v4-gpu research card (per-GPU rates; exact rows in research/gpu.json).
Replicate joined Cloudflare (announced 2025-11-17) and continues as a distinct brand with an unchanged API; no pricing change observed on the live pricing page as of 2026-09-29.

fleet.notes: Deployments expose min/max instances for autoscaling; API documents rate limits and contact for higher rates, not a fixed new-account GPU/VM allowance. Request-rate increase is distinct from fleet capacity; numeric aggregate quota and review SLA not established. Create-prediction API limited to 600 requests/min (other endpoints 3,000/min); accounts with granted credit and no payment method are limited to 1 req/s, max 6/min; stronger throttling as prepaid credit runs low. Higher limits via support.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

secret_proxy.quote: Once the model receives your secret, it’s removed from Replicate’s systems
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are Cog `Secret` typed prediction inputs passed into the model container (read with get_secret_value()); they are only redacted from logs/metadata/API responses. The secret does enter the container. No credential-injecting proxy.

isolation.quote: Cog is an open-source tool that lets you package machine learning models in a standard, production-ready container.
isolation.note: Models run as Docker containers (Cog); no VM/microVM boundary is documented per customer.

image_oci.quote: Or, build a Docker image for deployment: $ cog build -t my-classification-model
image_oci.note: You define your model with cog.yaml/predict.py, Cog builds a standard Docker image which is pushed and run on Replicate.

docker_inside.quote: Cog is an open-source tool that lets you package machine learning models in a standard, production-ready container.
docker_inside.note: not offered: the hosted platform runs your single Cog container image; no documented support for running Docker/containers nested inside that container.

nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU model-inference containers, not a VM/emulation platform; no /dev/kvm documented).

desktop.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (API-driven model hosting, no graphical desktop).

browser.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no managed/real browser is provided.

computer_use.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Replicate hosts model inference, not a screenshot/click desktop-driving API.

anti_bot.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU model-inference hosting, not a browser/scraping product).

captcha_solving.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: AWS Cloud Hosted Infrastructure and Data Hosting United States
egress_ip_type.note: Runs on hyperscaler/GPU-cloud datacenter infrastructure (AWS, CoreWeave, etc.); no residential/mobile egress documented.

ssh.quote: Replicate lets you build and scale AI products with your own custom models. You write the code, we handle the infrastructure orchestration and scaling.
ssh.note: not offered: models are invoked only via the HTTP/client-library prediction API; no SSH access to the running container is documented.

snapshot.quote: Auto-scaling: Scale from zero to hundreds of instances based on traffic
snapshot.note: No filesystem or memory snapshot/checkpoint feature is documented; instances scale to zero and cold-start fresh from the image.

snapshot_auto.quote: Auto-scaling: Scale from zero to hundreds of instances based on traffic
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: no automatic state snapshot/restore is documented.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Auto-scaling: Scale from zero to hundreds of instances based on traffic
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: no on-demand snapshot/checkpoint API is documented.

fork.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.
fork.note: not offered: no clone-a-running-machine feature; you deploy the same image to more replicas via autoscaling instead.

fork_running.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.

pause_resume.quote: Auto-scaling: Scale from zero to hundreds of instances based on traffic
pause_resume.note: not offered as a distinct pause/resume API; only scale-to-zero/autoscaling is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Auto-scaling: Scale from zero to hundreds of instances based on traffic
wake_on_request.note: Deployments/serverless models scale from zero automatically when a prediction request arrives (incurring a cold start).

persistent_disk.quote: Run arbitrary code and weights on high-end GPUs (A100s, H100s, B200s, and more) via API
persistent_disk.note: not offered: model containers are stateless inference workers; no documented persistent disk that survives stop/start outside the built image/weights.

volume_attach.quote: Run arbitrary code and weights on high-end GPUs (A100s, H100s, B200s, and more) via API
volume_attach.note: not offered: no attachable persistent volume feature documented.

volume_shared.quote: Run arbitrary code and weights on high-end GPUs (A100s, H100s, B200s, and more) via API

live_resize.quote: Hardware flexibility: Choose from multiple GPU architectures including NVIDIA A100s, H100s, T4s, and more. Switch hardware types without changing your code
live_resize.note: Hardware type is switched by redeploying, not resizing a live running instance; no live in-place resize documented.

agent_harnesses.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a model-hosting API, not a coding-agent sandbox with preinstalled harnesses).

harness_api.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

own_agent_api.quote: Run and fine-tune open-source models. Deploy custom models at scale. All with one line of code.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: Replicate hosts third-party/custom models via API; it does not offer its own browser/computer-use/research task agent.

lang_python.note: Official Python client library and Cog (Python-based model packaging) are first-party.

public_ipv4.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: access is via Replicate's HTTPS API/endpoints, not a per-machine public IPv4 address.

ingress_rules.quote: API tokens are used to authenticate your requests to the Replicate API.
ingress_rules.note: Access control is via API token auth, not user-configurable IP allowlists/security groups on exposed ports.

egress_allowlist.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: no provider-side outbound allow/deny-list or no-internet mode documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.

guest_firewall.quote: Cog is an open-source tool that lets you package machine learning models in a standard, production-ready container.
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is container-based (not a full VM/microVM with guest root), so in-guest firewall control is not applicable.

static_egress_ip.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed outbound IP feature documented.

windows.quote: Nvidia base images, efficient caching of dependencies, installing specific Python versions
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Cog/Replicate infrastructure is Linux/Docker-based GPU hosting.

macos.quote: Nvidia base images, efficient caching of dependencies, installing specific Python versions
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Linux GPU/CPU containers only.

arm64.note: not offered: published hardware tiers are x86 CPU and NVIDIA GPU (T4/L40S/A100/H100/H200); no ARM CPU option documented.

self_host.quote: You can deploy your packaged model to your own infrastructure, or to Replicate.
self_host.note: Cog, the packaging/runtime tool underlying Replicate's custom models, is explicitly self-hostable on your own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Deployments give you production-grade control over your model's infrastructure and provide private, dedicated API endpoints.
byoc.note: not offered: no managed-service-into-your-own-cloud-account option documented; self-hosting Cog yourself is separate from BYOC.

open_source.quote: Cog is an open-source tool that lets you package machine learning models in a standard, production-ready container.
open_source.note: Cog (github.com/replicate/cog) is open source (Apache-2.0); it underlies custom model deployment on Replicate, though the hosted Replicate platform itself is closed-source.

eu_data_residency.quote: AWS Cloud Hosted Infrastructure and Data Hosting United States
eu_data_residency.note: Primary infrastructure/data-hosting subprocessors are listed as United States; no EU-region residency option is documented.

max_session_h.quote: Always-on: Keep instances warm to eliminate cold starts
max_session_h.note: Dedicated/always-on deployment instances run continuously until you scale down or delete them; no documented maximum session duration.

sso.note: The account sign-in page only offers GitHub OAuth login; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO option is present there, and no docs page (Organizations, Security/API tokens, Enterprise) mentions SAML, OIDC, or single sign-on. Enterprise page lists priority support, SLAs, higher GPU limits, dedicated account manager, volume discounts, and custom-model help as enterprise perks, but not SSO.

cpu_class.quote: Unlike public models, most private models (with the exception of fast booting fine-tunes) run on dedicated hardware so you don't have to share a queue with anyone else. This means you pay for all the time instances of the model are online: the time they spend setting up; the time they spend idle, waiting for requests; and the time they spend active, processing your requests.
cpu_class.note: Custom-model (Cog) deployments and GPU serverless instances are billed as dedicated per-instance hardware (fixed vCPU/RAM/GPU counts per published hardware tier, e.g. cpu-small=1 vCPU/2GB, gpu-a100-large=10 vCPU/144GB) that is exclusively yours while online (setup+idle+active billed), not a shared/oversubscribed pool. No explicit CPU-sharing or burstable-baseline percentage is published, so this is inferred as dedicated across all listed pricing modes rather than confirmed per-mode with a distinct quote.
